title: Fifteen and a half months flat on his back
summary: Complications, a hip problem and repeated casts and ambulance trips stretch the recovery to fifteen and a half months, two and a half years out of work.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: No, it was longer than that. That's what the doctor said, 9 months. And complications did set in. He told me to lay in bed like, when I rolled over, roll like a log, on account of the spine. And he didn't put me in no
brace. The first doctor did -- had a brace made before I went in the hospital. I spent $40 for nothing.

And one Sunday at home, I was feeling good in the bed, and threw this leg over and turned the wrong way, and something hit me, and I started hurting down here, and I had the Sunday newspaper and I was trying to read it, and I was getting these pains; I said, 'Oh God' -- so I had to go through Sunday with all this ...

Monday I called the doctor, and he said he had to put me back in the hospital -- I told him what was happening, and I told him what I did. And I had to get an ambulance sent and go to the hospital. So they carried me to the hospital, and what happened, fluid had set in here from the spine, and hurt the hip -- I ended up having a hip operation eventually. But what they had to do, they had to mobilize me, and put me in a double spine/spiker cast, and pump the fluid out of here ... but it wouldn't last. And I'm telling it right. It did that and it relieved it -- and sent me back home. Then it happened and it built up the fluid again, and I had to go back in an ambulance. And every time you do that, it's $25 a walk.

This time was when they kept me in for about 4 days, and they put a double spike on me in the plaster room, and took it and split it up the side, and let me go on back without anything, and put it in the oven and bake it, and put straps on it where I have a top and bottom and you can take me
and flip me over, and you can take it off and rub my back or and THIS IS IN THE SUMMER MONTHS whatever, and I had me a scratcher, a stick that I had to stick down there and scratch where it itched.

For 15½ months I stayed in bed, flat on my back. Not 9. Complications did set in, and that was the hip. From that turn on that Sunday. Fifteen and a half months! That's the God's Gospel truth. And you take the 15½ months and the 4 months I had prior to that with two months of convalescent period and those other 4 months, and bunch it together, I'm out, really 2½ years. Ain't touched nothing, not making a living. But even Ben Barth didn't know how I made it. He called my wife up and he said, "Elizabeth, I'm leaving out of town now; if you need any money, now, Dick Big Boone has petty cash here, so if you need anything, call on him." Never asked for a quarter. Not a quarter.
